title: Sort Alternating Ascending and Descending List
description:
You are given the `head` of a singly linked list with a special alternating structure:
- Nodes at **odd 1-based positions** (`1st, 3rd, 5th, ...`) are sorted in **non-decreasing** order.
- Nodes at **even 1-based positions** (`2nd, 4th, 6th, ...`) are sorted in **non-increasing** order.

Sort the entire linked list in non-decreasing order and return its new head in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
Odd-positioned nodes are non-decreasing; even-positioned nodes are non-increasing.
hints: Split the list into two chains by parity of position: `asc` (odd positions) and `desc` (even positions).
Reverse the `desc` chain so both chains are sorted in non-decreasing order, then merge the two sorted lists in O(n) time.

examples.explanation: Odd chain is [10, 30, 50], even chain is [40, 20] which reverses to [20, 40]; merging gives [10, 20, 30, 40, 50].
Odd chain [1, 3, 5] and reversed even chain [2, 4, 6] merge to [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].
A single-node list [7] is already sorted.
